## Why This Is Asked
Real-time data quality is critical in lakehouse environments serving analytics at scale; this question probes practical cost-benefit modeling, risk assessment, and trade-offs for monitoring at scale.

## Key Concepts
- Data quality monitoring for streaming data (completeness, schema drift, anomalies)
- Multi-region cost model: capex vs opex, data ingestion/processing, metadata storage
- Business value levers: downstream analytics accuracy, SLA penalties avoided, faster insights
- Risk management: failure modes, mitigations, sensitivity analysis

## Code Example
```javascript
function breakEven(annualBenefit, annualCost) {
  return Math.ceil(annualCost / Math.max(annualBenefit, 1e-9));
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you set drift thresholds across regions and align them with SLAs?
- What instrumentation would you add to validate that the quality service improves downstream KPIs?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design an offline-first, privacy-conscious feature with clear cost drivers and trade-offs.

## Key Concepts
- Local token bucket and offline queuing
- Server quota reconciliation and idempotent requests
- Privacy/compliance considerations and rollout strategy

## Code Example
```javascript
class TokenBucket {
  constructor(capacity=100, refill=1){ this.capacity=capacity; this.tokens=capacity; this.refill=refill; this.last=Date.now(); }
  consume(n=1){ this.refresh(); if(this.tokens>=n){ this.tokens-=n; return true; } return false; }
  refresh(){ const now=Date.now(); const elapsed=(now-this.last)/1000; this.tokens = Math.min(this.capacity, this.tokens + elapsed*this.refill); this.last=now; }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would clock drift between device and server affect correctness and how would you mitigate it?
- What metrics would you monitor to decide go/no-go for rollout?
